130	
131	The one-run delay on cascades (phase 10 queues, phase 0 of the next run applies) removes any dependence on update order inside a run and gives every hop a minimum latency of 0.1 s, so a cascade reads as a sequence, never as an instant. Cross-loop coupling therefore has up to one run of latency per hop; nothing in this GDD assumes same-tick cross-loop consistency, so the VS-A stagger changes no rule.
132	
133	**LS-9 — Randomness is keyed, never counted.** The only stochastic rules are thaw-burst (C5) and, in VS-A, spark ignition (C9). Each draw is `rng_derive(world_seed, "graph.fail", (step_no << 20) | subject_id)` — the registry form is `mix64(world_seed XOR mix64(fnv64(stream_name)) XOR (counter * 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15))` — in GDScript the multiplier is written as the signed int `-7046029254386353131`, because 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 exceeds int64 and S0-b probes how the literal parses *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* with "counter (u64 stored in the owning block)" *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from command-simulation-layer)*; the Graph supplies the key as that counter, so the draw is a pure function of state, order-independent, and unchanged by weld, cut, restore or content added elsewhere. `subject_id < 2^20` is asserted (`MAX_GRAPH_NODES` 4096 and `MAX_GRAPH_EDGES` 8192 fit with room), leaving 43 bits of `step_no`. The clarification that "a stored running counter is one option; any owner-defined 63-bit key is valid" is a **routed amendment to the kernel's D.10**, not this GDD's rule (R4). *Alternative considered:* a sequential counter in the block — rejected (TD R10): a weld adds candidates and the draws of an unrelated derelict change. **Replay is exact and not steerable (user ruling D16 / X8, 2026-10-27)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: the Graph's physical failures and persisted counters replay exactly after a restore — a thaw-burst roll is a pure function of `(world_seed, step_no, subject_id)` and the persisted state, the Graph holds no restore-epoch input and reads no epoch (nor `PERCEPTION_OUT`, LS-22), and a reload therefore produces the identical roll, the identical burst or non-burst, at the identical step. Quitting or dying and reloading cannot reroll a Graph outcome. The threat draws of Attention and Horror Entities are re-keyed per restore epoch by their own owners (X8); that is their rule and the Graph neither supplies nor consumes the epoch; the epoch's storage and advance rules (delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13 / R14: a Continue of the newest QUIT generation keeps the epoch, death restores and other Continues advance it, held in Save/Load's per-slot `slot_epoch.bin` and never in a generation file) are Save/Load's and the kernel's, and change no Graph byte *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R13 / R14)*. **The thaw-burst roll window** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the roll window is persisted state, never inferred. When a FREEZE clears (phase 9, `T_room > FREEZE_OFF_MC`) the subject's `thaw_until_step` is set to `step_no + THAW_ROLL_STEPS` (default 100). In phase 8 of every later run with `step_no ≤ thaw_until_step` — exactly `THAW_ROLL_STEPS` runs — the subject rolls once: the draw is `rng_derive` as above and the burst happens iff `(draw & 0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF) % 1000 < BURST_P_PM`. A burst sets `hp = min(hp, BURST_HP_TO)` (default 3500, strictly between `HP_FAIL` and `LEAK_HP`, so a burst always starts a LEAK and never FAILs the pipe by itself — the first draft's `hp −= 3000` left a healthy 10000 pipe at exactly `HP_OK` 7000, which is no LEAK at all, so the "readable cost of growth" was invisible on the home ship), is ENDOGENOUS (the FREEZE pre-stage has held the D.11 gate open) and **sets `thaw_until_step` to 0: a success closes the window and the closure is persisted**, so a restore on any tick neither re-rolls a spent window nor forgets an open one. A window that runs out unspent is set to 0 on the first run with `step_no > thaw_until_step`; a re-freeze (forced FAILED again) closes it at once, and the next thaw opens a new one. P(burst in a window) = `1 − (1 − BURST_P_PM / 1000)^THAW_ROLL_STEPS` = 77.9 % at 15 ‰ and 100 steps, mean 6.7 s from thaw.
134	
135	**LS-10 — Failure lifecycle: six states, five severities.** States: `0 OK` (`hp ≥ HP_OK`, no forced mode), `1 DEGRADED` (`HP_FAIL < hp < HP_OK`; `eff` from D.4; hazard modes may be active; with none active the subject carries mode WORN, LS-11 — the module-body trace *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*), `2 FAILED` (`hp ≤ HP_FAIL` or `forced_mode ≠ 0`; no function; leaks continue; repairable), `3 DESTROYED` (`hp` = 0; permanent scrap; repair rejected `NOT_REPAIRABLE`; salvage then replace), `4 SALVAGED` (removed by `salvage_node`; tombstone slot; fluid ports `open_end`), `5 ABSENT` (never populated; inert; no ports connected; no descriptors). Severity `sev` 0..4 from D.4 (0 none; 1 trace — the weep, the flicker, the frost on the lagging; 2 minor; 3 major — hazard to nearby play, first `alarm_eligible` level; 4 critical — arcing, jetting, runaway), raised by hazard rules (breach `A_hole` ≥ 32 → 4; OVERLOAD `ρ` > 1000 → ≥ 1 from the first step over (LS-11) and `ρ` ≥ 1500 → 3; any forced mode → ≥ 3). Damage is monotonic per cause; repair raises `hp` only through `repair_step` up to `hp_cap`. The complete transition table is in *States and Transitions*.
136	
137	**LS-11 — Failure modes, triggers, pre-stages.** Mode ids: `1 LEAK` (DUCT, PIPE, tanks, reservoir; `hp < LEAK_HP`; clears when `hp ≥ LEAK_HP` or isolated by a closed VALVE upstream — isolated means the leak draws from nothing, the mode stays, the descriptor's `intensity_pm` is 0, and the subject loses no hp to leak wear while it is 0 (D.9) — a re-opened valve resumes the leak from the stored `hp` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from derelict-authoring-handmade-kits)*; the run the closed valve first drops the descriptor's `intensity_pm` to 0 stamps `isolated_at_step` = `step_no`, and the run the valve reopens (or the mode clears) resets it to 0 — the freeze point of the trail's `grow_steps`, LS-14 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*), `2 SHORT` (CABLE, CABLE_JUNCTION, LOAD; `hp ≤ HP_FAIL` — the FAILED boundary of LS-10, not a strict `<` — **while energised**: a CABLE is energised while an island at either of its end nodes holds a live source (`S + D` > 0, D.6), a CABLE_JUNCTION while an island at the far end of any incident cable does, a LOAD while `served_pm` > 0 (powered and drawing). Energised is NOT "carries watts": a FAILED cable has `cap` 0 and carries none, which is why the test is the live source behind it, the same test as the D.9 burn guard. Evaluated in phase 9 from the run's phase-2 island results and persisted as the mode flag, so it is set on the very run the subject lands on `HP_FAIL`; clears on repair (`hp > HP_FAIL`) or when no end island holds a live source (the upstream breaker opened, M9); never set on an authored dead cable or junction with no source behind it; a FAILED CABLE in SHORT keeps burning at `SHORT_BURN_BP_PER_STEP` until then, D.9) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — confirming review, blocker 1)*, `3 OVERHEAT` (REACTOR, LOAD machine, RESERVOIR; `T_mach > OVERHEAT_ON_MC` for `OVERHEAT_ON_STEPS`; clears at `T_mach < OVERHEAT_OFF_MC`; pre-stage: `T_mach` in HOT → sev 2 shimmer), `4 FREEZE` (coolant PIPE, RESERVOIR, liquid tanks; **pre-stage** sev 1 "frost on the lagging" at `T_room < FREEZE_WARN_MC`; forced FAILED at `T_room < FREEZE_ON_MC` once the D.11 gate is open; clears at `T_room > FREEZE_OFF_MC`, which opens the persisted thaw window and its burst rolls, LS-9) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, `5 BREACH` (HULL_SEGMENT, SEAM; `hp < BREACH_HP`, gated; pre-stage is the sev-1 hairline at `hp < HP_OK`; clears when `hp ≥ BREACH_HP`), `6 STARVE` (any powered node with `req_w > 0` and `served_pm < 1000`; a status, not a state change — it exists so the player can tell "off" from "broken"; its `sev` is the subject's D.4 `sev` (hp-derived, no STARVE-specific raise) floored at 1 while the status is live, so a live status is never a sev-0 descriptor, and it is never `alarm_eligible` (`alarm_capable(6)` is false, LS-13 (a)) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*), `7 OVERLOAD` (CABLE; `ρ > 1000`; sev 1 from the first step over — the hum climbs, the box warms — which is the warning that opens the window for the SHORT/FAILED that follows; `warn_since_step` is set on that first step, so the D.11 window opens there and not at the `HP_OK` crossing, and every D.11 figure is computed from this rule *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*), `8 SEVERED` (edge or port cut or salvaged with `open_end`; clears by `cap_port`), `9 SCRAM` (REACTOR; OVERHEAT sustained `OVERHEAT_SCRAM_STEPS` or fuel starve `FUEL_STARVE_STEPS`; clears by `reset_node` when `T_mach < OVERHEAT_OFF_MC` and fuel is present), `10 WORN` *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)* (any node or edge with `hp < HP_OK`, no mode 1–9 live on it and no patch on it — a patched subject emits PATCH_WEEP instead *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* — the un-modal trace of a worn module, the one a subject losing hp to duty wear or a GOUGE carries when nothing leaks, shorts or freezes; `sev` from D.4, `medium` NONE, `acoustic` NONE, never `alarm_eligible` (`alarm_capable(10)` is false by definition, LS-13 (a): a FAILED or DESTROYED module with no live mode 1-9 carries WORN at `sev` 3-4 and stays quiet whatever its gate) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; it is the module-body channel of LS-14 — readable on the sprite and the gauge, and on the inspect card only through the module's reduced output reading — the card carries no wear frame, word or mark *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from in-world-instruments-and-inspect-view)* — corruptible by Perception — and it counts toward `warn_since_step` like any `sev ≥ 1` descriptor; a subject emits WORN only while no mode 1–9 and no PATCH_WEEP is live on it, a hazard mode replaces it, and it clears at `hp ≥ HP_OK`). The closed-hatch descriptor `SEAL_STRAIN` is an OPENING descriptor (id 26, LS-14, D.14), the closed sibling of `AIRFLOW`, not a subject mode; it is never emitted for an OPENING with an EXTERIOR endpoint *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. **`PATCH_WEEP` (descriptor-only id 27)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* (creative-director ruling: a patch weeps): a subject with `hp_cap < HP_FULL` (patched), `hp < HP_OK` and no mode 1–9 live emits PATCH_WEEP instead of WORN — sev 1, on the **consequence channel**: `medium` by the subject's loop (GAS for a DUCT or O2_TANK, COOLANT or FUEL for a PIPE, RESERVOIR or FUEL_TANK, ELECTRIC for a CABLE, junction or LOAD, STRUCT for the rest), `acoustic` HISS / DRIP / TICK accordingly, `intensity_pm` 0 and never silenced by it (LS-14 provenance: no Graph-defined `intensity_pm`). It carries no flow — LEAK stays cleared at `hp ≥ LEAK_HP` — but it witnesses the patch itself: `hp_cap` is Graph truth, so a hallucinated "fully repaired" sprite or inspect card cannot hide a patch that is about to fail (P1, P4), and the sev-1 window it opens is the one the gated re-leak of R15 relies on. A patched hull or seam already carries the mode-5 STRUCT pre-stage and emits no PATCH_WEEP. Every mode that can force FAILED has a pre-stage at sev ≥ 1 that necessarily precedes it by more than `W_MIN_STEPS`, so LS-13 never has to invent a warning.
138	
139	**LS-12 — Cascades are physical chains, one hop per run, bounded.** No scripted "if A fails then B fails" exists; the chains below are what the numbers do, listed so that content, tests and the fairness audit can name them. Phase 10 applies at most `MAX_SPREAD_PER_STEP` (32) new forced modes per run in ascending subject id; the rest wait a run, so a failure front moves at a bounded speed — good for cost, better for dread.

### Core Rules

*Every rule below is a sim rule of the Graph owner module (`src/sim/graph/`), stated so that an implementer can write it and a tester can falsify it. Registry constants are cited by their registered name (`TICK_RATE`, `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS`, `STEP_BUDGET_MS`, `rng_derive`, `state_hash`, `hook_runs_this_tick`, `TILE_PX`); every constant this GDD introduces is written by the registry name it proposes (Section G marks the candidates). Type IDs are explicit, stable, checked unique at boot and never reused (R19). Where a rule records an alternative that was considered and rejected, the rejection is part of the rule: a later change must answer it.*

**LS-1 — One block, one determinism contract.** The Graph is exactly one persisted SIM state block, `graph.state` (owner Graph; `class` SIM; `persist` true; `persist_scope` WORLD; `scope` SHARED; `repl_hint` SHARED_SUMMARY; `schema_version` 1; `restore_after: [layout.state]`), registered by the Graph's composition-root call during BOOTING. It is a struct-of-arrays object (`GraphState extends RefCounted`; every field is underscore-prefixed and a lint forbids writes outside the four writer files `graph_mutators.gd`, `graph_propagate.gd`, `graph_restore.gd` (decode, validate, swap) and `graph_derived.gd` (non-persisted caches only), because GDScript has no private members) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: `PackedInt64Array` for conserved quantities and anything that can exceed 2^31, `PackedInt32Array` for ids, indices and basis points, `PackedByteArray` for enums and flags; the only strings are the append-only interned `def_table` (one `PackedStringArray` entry per distinct Item DB `def_id`, persisted in `canonical_bytes()` as a CSR pair — `def_off` (`PackedInt32Array`) and `def_utf8` (`PackedByteArray`) — and referenced from a node by an int32 `def_ix`, 0 = none) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; there are no per-node objects, no `Resource` for state or for saves, and no `Node` anywhere in the module (kernel H10; gdUnit4 exit 101 is impossible by construction). The contract: (a) **units** — gas in mGU (`GAS_SCALE` 1000; 1 GU is the amount giving 0.1 kPa in one tile), volume in tiles, pressure derived in dkPa (`STD_PRESSURE_DKPA` 1000), temperature in mC, power in W ≡ dJ per step, energy in dJ, liquids in mL, integrity in bp 0..10000 (`HP_FULL` 10000), fractions in permille, opening area in milli flow units on the gas path (`A_m` = 1000 × flow units, D.1), and a per-compartment gas maximum `n_max(c) = P_MAX × V_c × GAS_SCALE` with `P_MAX` 1500 dkPa (at most 3 × 10^8 mGU at `V` 200; 4.2 × 10^7 at standard pressure in the 42-tile cryo bay) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; (b) **zero floats** stored, hashed, replicated or used on the propagation path — a designer float in the data file is converted once at boot by `int(round(x × scale))` into the immutable `GraphTuning` and is not block state; (c) **store extensive, derive intensive** — `n_o2`, `n_inert`, `(T, t_rem)` as the energy pair `U = T × C + t_rem`, battery `stock` in dJ, liquid `stock_ml`, `hp`; `P`, `p_o2`, `o2_pm`, `served_pm`, `circ`, every descriptor and every cache are derived on read or in the run and never persisted — except the **hysteresis memory** of the three bands, of `pressure_trend` and of SEAL_STRAIN, which depends on the run before and is therefore persisted (`band_o2`, `band_p`, `band_t`, `p_prev`, two live bits per stored OPENING; LS-21) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; (d) **every flux is a non-negative magnitude with an explicit direction**, so integer division is applied only to non-negative operands and truncation is floor everywhere except the two signed remainder-carrying thermal steps, which truncate toward zero and carry the remainder (each file of `src/sim/graph/` opens with `@warning_ignore_start("integer_division")`, because every flux division is intentional integer division and would otherwise flood the editor with warnings; S0-b verifies that this annotation exists in 4.7.2 and silences the warning — the engine reference has no entry for it [UNV] — and if it does not, the fallback is the project setting `debug/gdscript/warnings/integer_division` set to Ignore for the module's directory, never a per-statement annotation on every flux) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; (e) **exact conservation** — each section carries persisted counters `vented_mgu` (gas lost to EXTERIOR), `radiated_dj` (net heat exchanged with the exterior sink through hull and radiators) and `spilled_cool_ml` (coolant lost from the loop), **plus the production and consumption counters `produced_mgu` (O2 the scrubber adds to the pool plus the inert make-up it supplies, D.5), `breathed_mgu` (O2 removed by M15), `produced_dj` (signed net heat injected, counted at its full value: the machine's whole `Q_src` — captured and uncaptured alike — the heater, BURN and CHILL footprints), `burned_uml` (fuel burned, in micro-millilitres: 10^6 µmL = 1 mL) and `spilled_heat_mdj` (heat carried out of the world by coolant that leaves the loop, in milli-dJ, signed because `t_cool` may be below 0)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; renamed from `burned_ul` and extended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; fuel lost from a pipe lands in the compartment's `fuel_puddle_ml`; the invariants — gas `Σ (n_o2 + n_inert) + Σ O2_TANK stock + vented_mgu + breathed_mgu + discarded_mgu + withdrawn_mgu − produced_mgu`; heat, in milli-dJ so that the equality is exact, `Σ_c (T_c × C_c + t_rem_c) + Σ_r (C_COOL × level_ml_r × t_cool_r + tc_rem_r) + 1000 × (radiated_dj − produced_dj) + spilled_heat_mdj` — the compartments' `U` **plus every RESERVOIR's heat store** (D.8 moves `Q_cap` and `Q_rad` into and out of that store, so it must be in the sum), where `spilled_heat_mdj` is credited in phase 5 at every coolant leak as `leak_ml × C_COOL × t_cool` (the coolant leaves at the loop's temperature) plus the reservoir's residual `tc_rem` on the run its `level_ml` reaches 0, and likewise for coolant discarded or withdrawn with a store (M6, M16, LS-16); coolant `Σ stock_ml + spilled_cool_ml + discarded_cool_ml + withdrawn_cool_ml`; fuel `10^6 × (Σ stock_ml + Σ fuel_puddle_ml + discarded_fuel_ml + withdrawn_fuel_ml) + burned_uml − Σ fuel_rem`, where `fuel_rem` (0..999,999 µmL per REACTOR) is the sub-mL part of the burn that `burned_uml` has already counted — worked check: a step at 2500 W burns 2500 × 120 = 300,000 µmL, so `burned_uml` and `fuel_rem` each gain 300,000 and the stock is unchanged; on the fourth step `fuel_rem` reaches 1,200,000, the stock loses 1 mL and `fuel_rem` becomes 200,000 with `burned_uml` 1,200,000, and `10^6 × (S − 1) + 1,200,000 − 200,000 = 10^6 × S` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; carried-over blocker, the factor is 10^6 and the counter is in µmL)* — are exact integer equalities over any number of steps **on a running ship with sources, sinks and crew active, not only with everything switched off**, and every test asserts them; (f) **every product the propagation code forms has documented operand maxima** and the boot assertion of D.13 refuses a build whose table violates `max_a × max_b < 2^62`; (g) **no `sqrt`, `exp`, `pow` or `sin` on the propagation path** — laws are linear or piecewise-linear integer tables, and per-step decay is written `x −= x × k_ppm / 10^6`; (h) **stability** — `Σ_j k_ij ≤ 1` per compartment (D.12), asserted at boot and re-checked by `can_join` at every weld; (i) **iteration is by ascending slot over dense arrays** and slot order equals ascending-id order at all times (slots are append-only within a session, removal tombstones, no compaction in MVP), so no result depends on a Dictionary's order and sim code never iterates a Dictionary; (j) **one explicit local-exchange pass per loop per run**, computed from a start-of-phase snapshot into accumulators and applied afterwards (Jacobi) — the snapshot is a double-buffered pair of arrays (`_cur` is read, `_next` is written, swapped when the phase ends), never a local alias: whether assigning a GDScript packed array to a `var` aliases it, copies it or copies on write is **not assumed anywhere in this document** (S0-a records it, ADR-LSG-01), and the working rule until it does is that a snapshot is taken only by an explicit `.duplicate()` or element copy into the preallocated scratch member and that writes go only through members of `GraphState` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* — with the source-depletion clamp resolved by scaling all outflows of an over-drawn node by `available / requested` in ascending edge id (the one exception is the VENT allocation of a short O2 pool, D.5, which is sequential-greedy in ascending node id because a vent is a draw on a shared store and the lower id is served first) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* — never an iterative or global solver, never catch-up ("we are behind, run two steps"): the kernel's lag policy drops time and the Graph must not re-add it. *Alternative considered:* two blocks (topology; flow/failure/atmosphere) as the kernel's Interactions row 1 says in the plural — rejected because a weld writes both and G4 wants one snapshot (R2; a routed wording fix "Blocks" → "Block" goes to the kernel owner). *Alternative considered:* SI units (mmol, J, mK) with an ideal-gas constant — rejected because a 2D game with tile volumes needs no gas constant and the worst product of the game units is 2 × 10^13 (D.13), which makes TD's two-stage temperature form and tank-pressure caveat moot (R1).

**LS-2 — Five loops, no sixth.** Loop ids: `0 NONE` (non-loop couplings), `1 O2`, `2 POWER`, `3 COOLANT`, `4 FUEL`, `5 INTEGRITY`. What "flow" means per loop is fixed here and nowhere else: **O2** — a pool of connected O2_TANK stocks (each with its def's `stock_cap`); SCRUBBER adds O2 (throttled to the free tank space) and offers inert make-up, VENT withdraws into its compartment (D.5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, consumers are bounded by `path_cap` (the bottleneck DUCT, seam or VALVE on the unique tree path, derived at topology refresh); **POWER** — an instantaneous island balance with no inventory except BATTERY, allocated by tier (D.6); edge load is the net flow through the edge on the island's tree — the served power below the edge minus what the sources below it deliver (D.6; one source at the root reduces to the served power below the edge) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* — and exists only for D.9; **COOLANT** — `circ` ‰ (D.8) says how much of the nominal heat exchange happens; heat is carried as the RESERVOIR's `(t_cool, tc_rem)` pair; **FUEL** — stock moves tank → burner limited by `path_cap`, burned per reactor output; **INTEGRITY** — static; `hp` is the store, STRUT load `ρ = load / cap` exists for VS-A redistribution and is not computed in MVP. Heat and pressure are **per-compartment atmosphere values** (LS-6), not loops: the O2 loop feeds compartments, the COOLANT loop moves heat between machines and radiators, and passive conduction and gas exchange between rooms are properties of OPENING edges. Anything proposed later (CO2, humidity, advection, fire) must either live per compartment or be out of scope; it may not become loop 6.

**LS-3 — Node kinds.** Stable ids: `1 COMPARTMENT`, `2 EXTERIOR` (one per world, node id 0, `P_EXT` 0 dkPa and `T_AMB_MC` −30000 in MVP, R14), `10 REACTOR`, `11 BATTERY`, `12 CABLE_JUNCTION` (holds `breaker_closed`), `13 LOAD` (with `subtype`; `HEATER` is a LOAD subtype with `waste_permille` 1000 — one in the MVP home-ship, R8 — whose effective request carries a stateless thermostat, D.7 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*), `20 SCRUBBER`, `21 O2_TANK`, `22 VENT`, `23 DUCT_JUNCTION`, `30 PUMP`, `31 RADIATOR`, `32 RESERVOIR`, `33 PIPE_JUNCTION`, `34 HEAT_EXCHANGER` (VS-A), `40 FUEL_TANK`, `41 FUEL_JUNCTION`, `42 FUEL_PORT` (VS-A), `50 HULL_SEGMENT`, `51 FRAME_NODE` (VS-A). Common persisted fields on every node: `id` (u32, never reused), `kind`, `section_id`, `def_ix` (index into the interned `def_table` of Item DB `def_id` strings, LS-1: 0 for COMPARTMENT/EXTERIOR/HULL_SEGMENT; the Item DB and `GRAPH_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_DEF` see the string) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, `state` (LS-10), `hp`, `hp_cap` (default `HP_FULL`), `forced_mode`, `forced_mode_next` (the cascade queue, LS-12), `fail_since_step`, `warn_since_step`, `mode_since_step`, `mode_key`, `isolated_at_step` (the three GA-T onset fields, LS-14: the step the subject's dominant descriptor entered its current mode and severity, that descriptor's `(mode << 3) | sev` as of the last run — hysteresis-class memory, persisted so a restore does not read a spurious change — and the step a closed valve first isolated it, 0 = not isolated) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*, `thaw_until_step` (the persisted thaw-burst roll window of a liquid-carrying subject, LS-9: 0 = closed) and a `has_warn` flag bit (a warning is running; `warn_since_step` is meaningful only while it is set, so a back-dated authored value ≤ 0 is valid, D.11) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, `patched_at_step`, `compartment_id` (where it physically sits — the reader's anchor), `ports[]`. Kind-specific persisted fields: REACTOR `out_w`, `fuel_rem`, `scram`, `starve_steps`; BATTERY `stock`; LOAD `req_w`, `tier`, `subtype`, `energised_at_step`; VENT `setpoint_pp`; PUMP `throttle_pm`; RESERVOIR `stock_ml`, `t_cool`, `tc_rem`; FUEL_TANK `stock_ml`; O2_TANK `stock`; HULL_SEGMENT `bound_compartment`, `exposed`, `tiles`, `fatigued`; COMPARTMENT per LS-6. Ports: `port_type_id`, `local_index`, `cap` (loop units per step, from the module def), `open_end`. Modules in the Item & Module Database declare `node_kind`, `ports[] = (port_type_id, cap, local_index)`, `tier`, `req_w`, `hp_start`, `waste_permille` and reference the port-type ids of LS-4 by number — the Item DB does not define them.

**LS-4 — Port types and the connectability matrix.** Encoding `loop × 100 + role` (roles: 1 SOURCE, 2 SINK, 3 STORE, 4 THRU); 9xx are non-loop couplings. `101 O2_SRC`, `103 O2_STORE`, `104 O2_THRU`; `201 PWR_SRC`, `202 PWR_SNK`, `203 PWR_STORE`, `204 PWR_THRU`; `301 CLT_HEAT_IN`, `302 CLT_HEAT_OUT`, `303 CLT_STORE`, `304 CLT_THRU`; `401 FUEL_SRC`, `402 FUEL_SNK`, `403 FUEL_STORE`, `404 FUEL_THRU`; `501 STR_ANCHOR`, `504 STR_THRU`; `901 ATMO_VENT` (node ↔ its compartment's gas), `902 THERMAL_COUPLE` (waste heat ↔ compartment, and the machine proxy), `903 HULL_FACE` (segment bounds a compartment and the exterior), `904 OPENING_FACE` (door, hatch or seam-gap side). `connectable(a, b)` is pure and used by data load and `can_join`: same loop; THRU joins anything of its loop; SRC–SNK, SRC–STORE, STORE–SNK allowed; SRC–SRC, SNK–SNK, STORE–STORE rejected (must go through a THRU); 301 and 302 attach only to 304; 904 only to 904; 901–903 never carry edges. Ids are append-only forever; a new port type is a new number.

**LS-5 — Edge kinds.** `1 DUCT` (O2; `cap` mGU/step, `len`, `exposed` — a hull-run duct whose leak goes to EXTERIOR instead of its compartment), `2 CABLE` (POWER; `cap` W), `3 PIPE` (COOLANT or FUEL by its `loop` field; `cap` mL/step), `4 STRUT` (INTEGRITY; VS-A), `5 VALVE` (O2/COOLANT/FUEL; `open`; closed is impassable and leak-isolating), `6 SEAM` (any loop; a loop edge crossing sections with `seam_id` and the seam's `q`; created only by `weld_join`), `7 OPENING` (no loop; `area` in flow units where 64 = one standard door aperture — the 96-px two-tile door, `A_HOLE_MAX` — so one unit is 1/64 of a door, not of a tile; `door_state`; `area` 0 is a sealed door *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from ship-section-and-layout-data-model)*). Breach holes and seam weeps are **virtual OPENINGs to EXTERIOR derived from `hp` and `(q, leak_bp)` each run** (D.2), never stored; a virtual opening counts toward a compartment's degree for D.1/D.12 exactly like a stored one. Common persisted edge fields: `id`, `kind`, `loop`, `a_node`, `a_port`, `b_node`, `b_port`, `hp`, `hp_cap`, `state`, `forced_mode`, `forced_mode_next`, `fail_since_step`, `warn_since_step`, `mode_since_step`, `mode_key`, `isolated_at_step` (as LS-3) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*, `thaw_until_step` and `has_warn` (as LS-3) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, `patched_at_step`, `seam_id` (0 = none), `capped`. `SeamRecord`: `seam_id`, `section_a`, `section_b`, `q`, `hp`, `leak_bp`, `edge_ids[]`, `opening_ids[]`, `L_seam`, `built_step`, `mode_since_step`, `mode_key` (the seam weep's onset is `built_step`, so `mode_since_step` starts there; a later BREACH pre-stage or `sev` change on the seam restamps it like any other subject; a seam has no `isolated_at_step`, because no valve isolates a weep) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*, `state`.

**LS-6 — Compartments, atmosphere and who owns what.** A COMPARTMENT is the Graph's model of a Layout room, keyed by Layout `room_id` (`layout_room_ref`). **Layout owns** room identity, polygon, `V` (tiles) and `exposed_tiles`; the Graph caches `V` and `exposed_tiles` as derived fields (not hashed; rebuilt in `post_restore`, which is why `restore_after: [layout.state]`). **The Graph owns** the atmosphere — `n_o2`, `n_inert`, `T`, `t_rem`, `fuel_puddle_ml` — and every opening/hatch `area` and `door_state`, every VALVE `open` and every breaker `closed`; Interaction issues the commands, the Graph publishes the mutators (R11; one writer per fact, kernel H3). Derived each run: `P`, `p_o2`, `o2_pm`, `band_o2`, `band_p`, `band_t`, `pressure_trend` (D.3); the previous run's three bands and `P` (`band_*`, `p_prev`) are the hysteresis memory and are persisted (LS-21) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, as are the three warn trackers `warn_since_o2/p/t` and `warn_bits` (LS-13 (b)) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. Scope of the physics (R14): pressure from `n` and `V` only (no T → P coupling), exterior always vacuum (`P_EXT` 0) with one radiative sink `T_AMB_MC`, no CO2, humidity or advected heat (heat moves only by conduction through openings and hull), no global rate dial — the constants are tuned, not scaled. The couplings the player reads are physical chains through these fields: scrubber (needs POWER) → pool → vent → `n_o2`; crew → `draw_air` → `n_o2`; opening → D.1 and D.7; breach → D.2 → D.1; machine → `THERMAL_COUPLE` → `Q_src_room`; coolant → D.8 → radiator; power loss → tier shedding → scrubbers/pumps/heater stop; cold → coolant FREEZE → burst on thaw; seam → weep; patch → vent and make-up → pressure recovers. **Air has two species and each is regulated to its own setpoint** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: `n_o2` to the vent's `SP` (default 210 dkPa) and `n_inert` to `SP_IN` = `STD_PRESSURE_DKPA − STD_O2_PP_DKPA` = 790 dkPa. Respiration removes O2 only, while every leak and every vent-to-space removes both species, so a room that has lost gas could never return to NORMAL pressure on O2 alone — the first draft's gap, in which total pressure could only fall and one breach damaged the ship for good (Pillar 5). The O2 comes from the pool (tank stock plus scrubber), the inert from the scrubber's demand-driven make-up (D.5, accounted in `produced_mgu`); both reach a room only through a vent with a live `path_cap`, so V5 and a cut duct still isolate a room. *Alternatives considered:* the literal "tanks and vents carry standard air" — rejected, it needs 4.76 mGU of pool per mGU of O2 against a 600 mGU/step vent, so one crew's respiration (300) would outrun the supply; a finite inert reserve in each tank — rejected for MVP by the user's confirmation of the scrubber make-up (2026-10-27, Open Question 30 resolved) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. *Alternative considered:* per-tile atmosphere so frost can creep tile by tile — rejected (TD R4): it multiplies N by 20–60 per room; spatial gradients are presentation derived from the true compartment values plus the leak anchor and `since_steps`, which still honours P1 because the frost reflects the true temperature.

**LS-7 — Bands and thresholds (the single source of truth).** The Graph publishes these; Suit, Failure & Trail, Instruments and Adaptive Audio consume them and never redefine them. Hysteresis `H_P` 5 dkPa / `H_T` 500 mC on re-entry (D.3). Registry candidates in bold are the constants Suit reads for damage onset: **`COLD_DMG_ONSET_MC` = −15000**, **`HEAT_DMG_ONSET_MC` = 45000**, **`HYPOXIA_PP` = 140**, **`DECOMP_P` = 400**; the O2 band edges 180 (NORMAL/THIN, registry candidate `O2_BAND_THIN_PP`) and 100 (HYPOXIC/ANOXIC, registry candidate `O2_BAND_ANOXIC_PP`) are published with them, read by name by the HUD & Suit Layer *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from hud-and-suit-layer)* (suit insulation shifts the cold onset; that is Suit's formula over this constant).

Time scale anchors (D.15): a door-sized breach decompresses a 20-tile room to LOW in 5.6 s; a pinhole takes 6 min to ANOXIC with one crew; a breached room frosts in 4 min and freezes its pipes in 12 min, while a healthy ship on one 500 W heater stays at COMFORT indefinitely and an unpowered one fogs breath at 6 min, frosts at 13 and — with no hull hole at all — freezes its liquid pipes at 41 min (FREEZE pre-stage at 23 min), the intentional dark-ship clock *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; one battery cell runs the life-critical tiers for 6 min.

**LS-8 — Three hooks, twelve phases, fixed order.** The Graph registers three real step hooks at divisor 6 with offsets 0 (power), 2 (atmo) and 4 (failure) — **the staggered baseline** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* — still chained by `after:` (kernel CR-3, `hook_runs_this_tick` = `(T mod divisor) == offset`) — the two chain edges (`graph.propagate.atmo` after `.power`, `.failure` after `.atmo`) are declared `{hook_id, tolerates_stale: true}`: at offsets 0 / 2 / 4 each pair never runs in one tick and CR-3 warns on an undeclared never-co-running edge; the edge still fixes the resolved order. A same-tick reader shares the offset of the hook it follows (Suit (6, 2) with `.atmo`, Attention (6, 0) with `.power`); a reader at another offset (Sanity (12, 0)) declares `tolerates_stale` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*: `graph.propagate.power` (root; phases 0–3), `graph.propagate.atmo` (`after: [graph.propagate.power]`; phases 4–7), `graph.propagate.failure` (`after: [graph.propagate.atmo]`; phases 8–11). One run = one step = `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` 6 ticks = 0.1 s; `step_no = ⌊T / 6⌋` for all three hooks (they run on T = 6n, 6n + 2 and 6n + 4), persisted as the per-hook cursors `last_step_power`, `last_step_atmo` and `last_step_failure` (`last_step_no` is the last step whose failure hook has run, i.e. the last complete step) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Dependents name the hook they read: Suit vitals `after: graph.propagate.atmo`, Attention `after: graph.propagate.power`; Failure & Trail is presentation and reads dirty keys. Because the kernel has no alias concept, this is CR-3 as written. The stagger is the **baseline**, not a fallback *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the three hooks spread over three of the six ticks, so no tick carries more than one Graph hook (the home ship alone is estimated at 825 µs per step at the review's coefficients against a 0.5 ms share, so the unstaggered tick cannot meet the share; the coefficients are [UNV] and S0-f decides the number, not the structure). A reader must share the offset of the hook it follows or see a run-old value (kernel edge case): Suit's vitals register at offset 2, Attention at 0, Emitter State reads at offset 4 — cross-GDD registrations, applied 2026-10-28: Suit SE-1/A12/AC-SE-2/AC-SE-3 at (6, 2), Attention (6, 0), Emitter State reads after `.failure`, the kernel rows and fixtures, the Overlay per-hook-tick sample, Assembly tick-order note, Interaction lag note, Sanity stale edges (Open Question 41). **Data-only revert:** if S0-f shows the stagger buys nothing, the three Graph offsets and Suit become 0 (two registrations); Suit A12 compares offsets, not values, so both states boot; no Graph rule changes *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. **Topology refresh is one idempotent function** run at the head of whichever Graph hook runs first after a structural mutator (M1-M5): power (`T mod 6` = 0), atmo (2) or failure (4), not only at phase 1; a weld, cut, discard or install applied in P2 on any tick is seen whole by the next Graph hook and no hook reads a half-applied topology; zero cost while `topo_dirty` is clear *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. The order of effects within a step is unchanged (power, then atmo, then failure, then the next step's phase 0), so no rule of this document depends on the stagger. The phases:

Cross-loop coupling therefore has up to one run of latency per hop; nothing in this GDD assumes same-tick cross-loop consistency, so the VS-A stagger changes no rule.

**LS-9 — Randomness is keyed, never counted.** The only stochastic rules are thaw-burst (C5) and, in VS-A, spark ignition (C9). Each draw is `rng_derive(world_seed, "graph.fail", (step_no << 20) | subject_id)` — the registry form is `mix64(world_seed XOR mix64(fnv64(stream_name)) XOR (counter * 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15))` — in GDScript the multiplier is written as the signed int `-7046029254386353131`, because 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 exceeds int64 and S0-b probes how the literal parses *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* with "counter (u64 stored in the owning block)" *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from command-simulation-layer)*; the Graph supplies the key as that counter, so the draw is a pure function of state, order-independent, and unchanged by weld, cut, restore or content added elsewhere. `subject_id < 2^20` is asserted (`MAX_GRAPH_NODES` 4096 and `MAX_GRAPH_EDGES` 8192 fit with room), leaving 43 bits of `step_no`. The clarification that "a stored running counter is one option; any owner-defined 63-bit key is valid" is a **routed amendment to the kernel's D.10**, not this GDD's rule (R4). *Alternative considered:* a sequential counter in the block — rejected (TD R10): a weld adds candidates and the draws of an unrelated derelict change. **Replay is exact and not steerable (user ruling D16 / X8, 2026-10-27)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: the Graph's physical failures and persisted counters replay exactly after a restore — a thaw-burst roll is a pure function of `(world_seed, step_no, subject_id)` and the persisted state, the Graph holds no restore-epoch input and reads no epoch (nor `PERCEPTION_OUT`, LS-22), and a reload therefore produces the identical roll, the identical burst or non-burst, at the identical step. Quitting or dying and reloading cannot reroll a Graph outcome. The threat draws of Attention and Horror Entities are re-keyed per restore epoch by their own owners (X8); that is their rule and the Graph neither supplies nor consumes the epoch; the epoch's storage and advance rules (delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13 / R14: a Continue of the newest QUIT generation keeps the epoch, death restores and other Continues advance it, held in Save/Load's per-slot `slot_epoch.bin` and never in a generation file) are Save/Load's and the kernel's, and change no Graph byte *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R13 / R14)*. **The thaw-burst roll window** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the roll window is persisted state, never inferred. When a FREEZE clears (phase 9, `T_room > FREEZE_OFF_MC`) the subject's `thaw_until_step` is set to `step_no + THAW_ROLL_STEPS` (default 100). In phase 8 of every later run with `step_no ≤ thaw_until_step` — exactly `THAW_ROLL_STEPS` runs — the subject rolls once: the draw is `rng_derive` as above and the burst happens iff `(draw & 0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF) % 1000 < BURST_P_PM`. A burst sets `hp = min(hp, BURST_HP_TO)` (default 3500, strictly between `HP_FAIL` and `LEAK_HP`, so a burst always starts a LEAK and never FAILs the pipe by itself — the first draft's `hp −= 3000` left a healthy 10000 pipe at exactly `HP_OK` 7000, which is no LEAK at all, so the "readable cost of growth" was invisible on the home ship), is ENDOGENOUS (the FREEZE pre-stage has held the D.11 gate open) and **sets `thaw_until_step` to 0: a success closes the window and the closure is persisted**, so a restore on any tick neither re-rolls a spent window nor forgets an open one. A window that runs out unspent is set to 0 on the first run with `step_no > thaw_until_step`; a re-freeze (forced FAILED again) closes it at once, and the next thaw opens a new one. P(burst in a window) = `1 − (1 − BURST_P_PM / 1000)^THAW_ROLL_STEPS` = 77.9 % at 15 ‰ and 100 steps, mean 6.7 s from thaw.

**LS-10 — Failure lifecycle: six states, five severities.** States: `0 OK` (`hp ≥ HP_OK`, no forced mode), `1 DEGRADED` (`HP_FAIL < hp < HP_OK`; `eff` from D.4; hazard modes may be active; with none active the subject carries mode WORN, LS-11 — the module-body trace *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*), `2 FAILED` (`hp ≤ HP_FAIL` or `forced_mode ≠ 0`; no function; leaks continue; repairable), `3 DESTROYED` (`hp` = 0; permanent scrap; repair rejected `NOT_REPAIRABLE`; salvage then replace), `4 SALVAGED` (removed by `salvage_node`; tombstone slot; fluid ports `open_end`), `5 ABSENT` (never populated; inert; no ports connected; no descriptors). Severity `sev` 0..4 from D.4 (0 none; 1 trace — the weep, the flicker, the frost on the lagging; 2 minor; 3 major — hazard to nearby play, first `alarm_eligible` level; 4 critical — arcing, jetting, runaway), raised by hazard rules (breach `A_hole` ≥ 32 → 4; OVERLOAD `ρ` > 1000 → ≥ 1 from the first step over (LS-11) and `ρ` ≥ 1500 → 3; any forced mode → ≥ 3). Damage is monotonic per cause; repair raises `hp` only through `repair_step` up to `hp_cap`. The complete transition table is in *States and Transitions*.

Energised is NOT "carries watts": a FAILED cable has `cap` 0 and carries none, which is why the test is the live source behind it, the same test as the D.9 burn guard. Evaluated in phase 9 from the run's phase-2 island results and persisted as the mode flag, so it is set on the very run the subject lands on `HP_FAIL`; clears on repair (`hp > HP_FAIL`) or when no end island holds a live source (the upstream breaker opened, M9); never set on an authored dead cable or junction with no source behind it; a FAILED CABLE in SHORT keeps burning at `SHORT_BURN_BP_PER_STEP` until then, D.9) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — confirming review, blocker 1)*, `3 OVERHEAT` (REACTOR, LOAD machine, RESERVOIR; `T_mach > OVERHEAT_ON_MC` for `OVERHEAT_ON_STEPS`; clears at `T_mach < OVERHEAT_OFF_MC`; pre-stage: `T_mach` in HOT → sev 2 shimmer), `4 FREEZE` (coolant PIPE, RESERVOIR, liquid tanks; **pre-stage** sev 1 "frost on the lagging" at `T_room < FREEZE_WARN_MC`; forced FAILED at `T_room < FREEZE_ON_MC` once the D.11 gate is open; clears at `T_room > FREEZE_OFF_MC`, which opens the persisted thaw window and its burst rolls, LS-9) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, `5 BREACH` (HULL_SEGMENT, SEAM; `hp < BREACH_HP`, gated; pre-stage is the sev-1 hairline at `hp < HP_OK`; clears when `hp ≥ BREACH_HP`), `6 STARVE` (any powered node with `req_w > 0` and `served_pm < 1000`; a status, not a state change — it exists so the player can tell "off" from "broken"; its `sev` is the subject's D.4 `sev` (hp-derived, no STARVE-specific raise) floored at 1 while the status is live, so a live status is never a sev-0 descriptor, and it is never `alarm_eligible` (`alarm_capable(6)` is false, LS-13 (a)) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*), `7 OVERLOAD` (CABLE; `ρ > 1000`; sev 1 from the first step over — the hum climbs, the box warms — which is the warning that opens the window for the SHORT/FAILED that follows; `warn_since_step` is set on that first step, so the D.11 window opens there and not at the `HP_OK` crossing, and every D.11 figure is computed from this rule *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*), `8 SEVERED` (edge or port cut or salvaged with `open_end`; clears by `cap_port`), `9 SCRAM` (REACTOR; OVERHEAT sustained `OVERHEAT_SCRAM_STEPS` or fuel starve `FUEL_STARVE_STEPS`; clears by `reset_node` when `T_mach < OVERHEAT_OFF_MC` and fuel is present), `10 WORN` *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)* (any node or edge with `hp < HP_OK`, no mode 1–9 live on it and no patch on it — a patched subject emits PATCH_WEEP instead *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* — the un-modal trace of a worn module, the one a subject losing hp to duty wear or a GOUGE carries when nothing leaks, shorts or freezes; `sev` from D.4, `medium` NONE, `acoustic` NONE, never `alarm_eligible` (`alarm_capable(10)` is false by definition, LS-13 (a): a FAILED or DESTROYED module with no live mode 1-9 carries WORN at `sev` 3-4 and stays quiet whatever its gate) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; it is the module-body channel of LS-14 — readable on the sprite and the gauge, and on the inspect card only through the module's reduced output reading — the card carries no wear frame, word or mark *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from in-world-instruments-and-inspect-view)* — corruptible by Perception — and it counts toward `warn_since_step` like any `sev ≥ 1` descriptor; a subject emits WORN only while no mode 1–9 and no PATCH_WEEP is live on it, a hazard mode replaces it, and it clears at `hp ≥ HP_OK`). The closed-hatch descriptor `SEAL_STRAIN` is an OPENING descriptor (id 26, LS-14, D.14), the closed sibling of `AIRFLOW`, not a subject mode; it is never emitted for an OPENING with an EXTERIOR endpoint *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. **`PATCH_WEEP` (descriptor-only id 27)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* (creative-director ruling: a patch weeps): a subject with `hp_cap < HP_FULL` (patched), `hp < HP_OK` and no mode 1–9 live emits PATCH_WEEP instead of WORN — sev 1, on the **consequence channel**: `medium` by the subject's loop (GAS for a DUCT or O2_TANK, COOLANT or FUEL for a PIPE, RESERVOIR or FUEL_TANK, ELECTRIC for a CABLE, junction or LOAD, STRUCT for the rest), `acoustic` HISS / DRIP / TICK accordingly, `intensity_pm` 0 and never silenced by it (LS-14 provenance: no Graph-defined `intensity_pm`). A patched hull or seam already carries the mode-5 STRUCT pre-stage and emits no PATCH_WEEP. Every mode that can force FAILED has a pre-stage at sev ≥ 1 that necessarily precedes it by more than `W_MIN_STEPS`, so LS-13 never has to invent a warning.

154	**LS-13 — The fairness gate is a sim rule.** `W_MIN_WARNING_S` = 10 (`W_MIN_STEPS` 100) is a hard rule of this block (R7) *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN: raised from 8 s to 10 s)*: an **endogenous** transition to FAILED or DESTROYED (node or edge) and a hull or seam LEAK → BREACH escalation require that the subject has emitted a descriptor of `sev ≥ 1` for at least 100 consecutive steps (`warn_elapsed`, D.11). While the gate is closed `hp` is floored at `HP_FAIL + 1` (or `BREACH_HP` for the breach case) and the excess damage is discarded. **Exogenous** causes bypass the gate: player verbs (cut, vent, salvage, overload by breaker — the damage of the `INRUSH_STEPS` after a breaker close is tagged EXOGENOUS, D.9) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, footprint-channel RUPTURE and GOUGE, and `apply_damage` with `cause = EXOGENOUS`. **Exported requirement — exogenous sources carry their own tell** *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*: the gate protects against the sim, not against agency, so it never delays an exogenous apply; every non-player exogenous source — M17 RUPTURE and GOUGE from Horror Entities and M17 STRESS from Attention (its only caller) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from horror-entities, attention-system)*, and environmental M18 `apply_damage(…, EXOGENOUS)` — must therefore be preceded by that system's own Pillar 2 tell of 10–30 s (the stalk, the scrape, the rhythm change) stated in its GDD. The Graph neither emits nor checks that tell; a source that applies exogenous damage with no tell is in breach of this requirement, which the (review) criterion in Section H discharges. Player death is Suit's rule; the Graph guarantees that the *cause* — the room's band, the module's failure — was warned. `alarm_eligible` on a descriptor is true only for an alarm-capable mode (LS-13 (a) below), at `sev ≥ ALARM_SEV_MIN` (3 by default) **and** with the gate open *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, so alarm-class presentation (the rotating sweep) is never the first channel; exported requirement to Perception Filter, Sanity & Hallucination and Failure & Trail (R17): no consumer may suppress a consequence-channel descriptor's acoustic or physical channel (LS-14: any descriptor with `medium ≠ NONE`; a WORN descriptor is module-body and is the Filter's to corrupt *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*), a filter may add or alter sprites and gauges but never remove a hiss, a cold or a thin-air, and `alarm_eligible` never first. **Alarm capability, compartment gate, scope, exemption** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; Blocker 2: the owner adds the surface, the consumers' ruled behaviour — Suit `suit.alarm`, HUD sixth mark, Audio annunciator — is the spec, G6)*: **(a) Capability.** `alarm_capable(mode)` is true for modes 1 LEAK, 2 SHORT, 3 OVERHEAT, 4 FREEZE, 5 BREACH, 7 OVERLOAD, 8 SEVERED, 9 SCRAM and 20-23, and FALSE BY DEFINITION, whatever `ALARM_SEV_MIN` (range 2-4), for 6 STARVE, 10 WORN, 24 AIRFLOW, 25 PUDDLE, 26 SEAL_STRAIN and 27 PATCH_WEEP *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* (creative-director ruling under G6 / R20: 10 WORN and 6 STARVE leave the capable set). WORN is the module-body channel (`medium` NONE, `acoustic` NONE, corruptible by the Filter) and takes `sev` 3-4 from D.4 on any FAILED or DESTROYED module with no live hazard mode (a FAILED scrubber at `hp` 2000 that is switched off, `req_w` 0, is WORN `sev` 4), so keying the alarm on it would sound the klaxon, the Suit `suit.alarm` bit and the HUD sixth mark for a dead, silent fault through a channel the Filter may corrupt — a breach of P2 and of the two-channel rule. STARVE is the status that tells "off" from "broken" (every load on a dead branch carries it, so a FAILED load on an unserved branch, the Derelict A boarding case, carries STARVE and not WORN; the commonest cause is a breaker the player opened): it is a status, not a hazard to nearby play, and its `sev` is the subject's D.4 `sev` floored at 1 while it is live (LS-11). A module with no live hazard therefore never raises the ship alarm, even with an open gate (including an authored back-dated `warn_since_step`); the same module with a live mode 1-5 or 7-9 (a forced FREEZE, a LEAK, a BREACH, or SHORT on a FAILED load that is powered and drawing) does, at `sev` >= `ALARM_SEV_MIN` once its gate is open — WORN yields to the hazard mode (LS-11), so the alarm of a worn-out machine begins when its fault becomes a hazard. OPENING descriptors therefore need no gate input; the alarm presentation of a decompression rides the room's ATMO_DECOMP (LS-14 already says so). **(b) Compartment gate input.** Each compartment carries three persisted warn trackers, one per band state machine: `o2` (drives ATMO_THIN: THIN 1, HYPOXIC 3, ANOXIC 4), `p` (ATMO_DECOMP: LOW 2, DECOMP 3, VACUUM 4) and `t` (ATMO_COLD: COOL 1, FROST 2, FREEZING 3, DEEP_COLD 4; ATMO_HOT: HOT 2, SCORCH 4; exclusive). Tracker x = `warn_since_x` (i32) plus bit x of `warn_bits` (u8). In phase 9, compartment id ascending after nodes and edges, with `sev_x` = severity of the descriptor `band_x` currently maps to (0 if none): `sev_x` ≥ 1 and bit clear → set the bit, `warn_since_x` = `step_no`; `sev_x` = 0 → clear the bit, `warn_since_x` = 0. A worsening (THIN → HYPOXIC) does not reset the window; any return to OK does (the band hysteresis `H` is the only debounce). `warn_elapsed_x` = `step_no − warn_since_x` if the bit is set, else 0; `gate_open` = `warn_elapsed_x ≥ W_MIN_STEPS` (100). The gate delays no physics (a compartment has no `hp`); it only withholds `alarm_eligible`. M1 may supply back-dated `warn_since_x` for an authored derelict room as for nodes; absent one the tracker opens on the first run, so a room authored thin or empty is silent for its first 100 steps and the body cues come first (R7/R17). Cost: three compares per compartment per run. **(c) Alarm scope = the loop set.** The Graph publishes one pure read `alarm_sections() -> PackedInt32Array`: ascending, duplicate-free `section_id`s (`section_of(compartment_id)` of the descriptor) owning at least one descriptor with `alarm_eligible` true in the last committed run; empty = no alarm. The "seat's loop set" (Suit SE-29, HUD HS-25 / OQ-HS-79) and the "listener's body" (Audio AA-27) are ONE predicate: all six loops (0..5, compartment descriptors included) of every section of the body the seat or listener stands on; a consumer tests `alarm_sections()` ∩ `sections_of(body_of(section_id))` non-empty with Layout's pure reads. Consequences: a derelict breach IS in the seat's loop set (OQ-HS-79 (1): yes); a home-ship fault alarms a seat on the home body; a fault on another body does not. The read names no loop or place beyond sections the consumer already knows. **(d) CX-A1 — exemption.** The Graph's annunciator `ann` (Audio AA-27) is gated by `alarm_eligible`; Attention's breach-entry `attn` cadence (Attention AT-18, Audio AA-20) is Attention's own tell-contract event, not a Graph descriptor, and is preceded by a tell of at least `TELL_MIN_TICKS` by construction, so it is exempt from this gate and is never "the first warning". This closes CX-A1 (the consumers' alarm-gate lints, in the Audio and Attention GDDs, carry the exemption). *Alternative considered:* a content guideline rather than a sim gate — rejected (GD Q5): deaths must have a nameable cause in every build, not only in well-authored content.

The "seat's loop set" (Suit SE-29, HUD HS-25 / OQ-HS-79) and the "listener's body" (Audio AA-27) are ONE predicate: all six loops (0..5, compartment descriptors included) of every section of the body the seat or listener stands on; a consumer tests `alarm_sections()` ∩ `sections_of(body_of(section_id))` non-empty with Layout's pure reads. Consequences: a derelict breach IS in the seat's loop set (OQ-HS-79 (1): yes); a home-ship fault alarms a seat on the home body; a fault on another body does not. The read names no loop or place beyond sections the consumer already knows. **(d) CX-A1 — exemption.** The Graph's annunciator `ann` (Audio AA-27) is gated by `alarm_eligible`; Attention's breach-entry `attn` cadence (Attention AT-18, Audio AA-20) is Attention's own tell-contract event, not a Graph descriptor, and is preceded by a tell of at least `TELL_MIN_TICKS` by construction, so it is exempt from this gate and is never "the first warning". This closes CX-A1 (the consumers' alarm-gate lints, in the Audio and Attention GDDs, carry the exemption). *Alternative considered:* a content guideline rather than a sim gate — rejected (GD Q5): deaths must have a nameable cause in every build, not only in well-authored content.

**LS-14 — `FailureDescriptor` schema.** Derived each run in phase 11 from state (only `fail_since_step`, `warn_since_step` and the three GA-T onset fields `mode_since_step`, `mode_key` and `isolated_at_step` are persisted *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*); the Graph emits semantics, never visuals.

220	**LS-15 — Seams: a weld moves nothing.** Sections are instantiated into the one world graph when they exist (`instantiate_section`); ids come from the block's `next_*` counters in template order, so a weld **only adds edges** and never renumbers. A weld plan is plain data `{ section_a, section_b, pairs[]: (node_a, port_a, node_b, port_b, loop), openings[]: (comp_a, comp_b, area_max), L_seam, q }` validated by the pure query `can_join(plan)` with the closed reason set `SECTION_UNKNOWN`, `SECTION_NOT_LOADED` (dormant counts as not loaded), `SOCKET_OCCUPIED`, `PORT_INCOMPAT`, `PORT_ABSENT` (ABSENT, DESTROYED or SALVAGED endpoint), `SEAM_LIMIT` (> `MAX_SEAMS_PER_SECTION` 8), `ALREADY_JOINED`, `CAPACITY` (`MAX_GRAPH_NODES` 4096 / `MAX_GRAPH_EDGES` 8192), `POWER_CYCLE` (the cable pairs would close a cycle in POWER wiring — R12: islands are trees, cycles are rejected here and at data load, VS-A may lift it), `STABILITY` (D.12). It returns the fully resolved plan (slot indices, edge count) and informational `surge[]` per sub-edge (D.14), flagging an opening whose `|ΔP| > WELD_DP_WARN` 300 dkPa — **a warning, never a reject**; the warning is diegetic: the closed hatch's own `SEAL_STRAIN` descriptor (CREAK at the rim, rim frost when `|ΔT| > HATCH_DT_FROST_MC`; D.14, LS-14) and the corruptible gauge. `surge[]` reaches the player only through those tells and instruments — never as a number in a weld preview or any other UI; Assembly's preview may consume `surge[].warn` to pick a diegetic cue, not to print the value *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*. `weld_join` then only appends the pre-validated edges, writes the SeamRecord, sets every sub-edge **disconnected** (R9: opening `area` 0, pipe and duct valves closed, cable breaker open), bumps `topology_version` and marks `T` + `S/<seam_id>` + `SEC/<a>` + `SEC/<b>`; nothing in it can fail, so CR-9's infallible apply holds. Connecting is then three lit verbs (`set_opening_area`, `set_valve`, `set_breaker`), each with its own surge read-out. The seam weeps through `A_seam_m` from the step it exists (D.2, D.14) until wear-in or a seam PATCH (M7; V11 SEAL_SEAM is the VS-A form) — the weld's own P1 tell. **Structural half, returns, seam read** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from modular-ship-assembly, ship-section-and-layout-data-model)*: `can_join_static(plan)` is published as a pure query returning the first failing reason of the nine structural reasons in LS-15 order — `SECTION_UNKNOWN`, `SECTION_NOT_LOADED`, `SOCKET_OCCUPIED`, `PORT_INCOMPAT`, `SEAM_LIMIT`, `ALREADY_JOINED`, `CAPACITY`, `POWER_CYCLE`, `STABILITY` — reading no node `hp`, `state`, `forced_mode` or `served_pm` and computing no `surge[]`; `can_join` adds `PORT_ABSENT` (a node-state read) at its LS-15 position and the `surge[]` read-out. `weld_join` returns `{seam_id, opening_ids[]}`; `seam_view(seam_id)` → `{state, sub_edges[{kind, id}], leak_bp, opening_ids[], cut_sides[]}` is pure *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, routed from modular-ship-assembly D54 / ASK G10)*: `cut_sides` is empty unless the seam is `CUT` with boundary RAGGED, and then holds one entry per side, `{section_id, cut_holes[{cid, a_hole}], uncapped_open_ends}`, where `cid` is the compartment carrying that side's A_CUT virtual hole (one per former opening), `a_hole` is the hole's CURRENT D.2 area (24 at `hp` 2500; 0 once a Vertical Slice plate install or repair closes it) and `uncapped_open_ends` is the count of that side's fluid ports still `open_end`. It is derived from the hull-stub records and port flags already in `graph.state` (no new persisted field; the SeamRecord tombstone keeps the cut hole ids). The Graph has no keep / leave notion: it returns BOTH sides keyed by `section_id`, and Assembly picks the keep sides from Layout's `keep_sections`. A welded section keeps its `kind` and `rate_pm` (LS-17, LS-25): M2 does not promote a DERELICT section, so a cut restores nothing. An as-welded seam is **not quiet**: it moves nothing between the sections, but it weeps (HISS at the seam) from its first run until wear-in brings `leak_bp` to 0 at period 100 or V1 patches it — the weep tapers **linearly with `leak_bp`** to a cliff at 0 (D.14), not a function of `q`. **Intended seam clock** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: a default weld (`q` 850, `L_seam` 3) is tight at period 100 = 16.7 min; the weld-side bay loses about 20 % of its gas over that time if nothing compensates: its total pressure never leaves NORMAL (D.15 SEAM-WEEP), but with its vent isolated its O2 band enters THIN at about step 4,325 (7.2 min) and stays there until the vent runs or the seam is sealed — a deliberate sev-1 tell of the unvented bay, absent with the vent live; V1 PATCH on the seam ends the weep at once (M7 sets `leak_bp` to 0 on a SEAM) and a running vent makes the gas up. The weep carries no LEAK wear (D.9) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. *Alternative considered:* opening the seam at weld with a hard reject above a `ΔP` limit (SD OQ-13) — rejected (R9): it created a vacuum-section soft-lock and a loop-surge leak; the disconnected start removes both and makes every connection a readable choice.
221	
222	**LS-16 — Cuts, only along seams.** `cut_detach(seam_id, boundary_mode)` is atomic in one P2 apply. `SEALED` (cut at a bulkhead or hatch): the seam's OPENINGs are removed, its loop sub-edges tombstoned, both sides' fluid ports `capped` — nothing leaks. `RAGGED` (cut through the weld): for each former opening a virtual hole of `A_CUT` 24 is attached to each side's compartment as a hull stub with `hp` 2500 (sev 4 — D.4 gives sev 4 at `hp` ≤ 2500 — BREACH, exogenous — no gate) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G4)*, and each side's fluid ports become `open_end` (SEVERED) leaking at `OPEN_END_RATE_PM` (500 ‰ of port cap per step) until `cap_port`. **The two RAGGED hazards are independent** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, routed from modular-ship-assembly D54)*: `cap_port` (M12) closes a fluid port's hiss only and never changes the hull hole. The A_CUT hull stub (`hp` 2500, `a_hole` 24) has no subject in the MVP: no verb patches, caps or repairs it, so the cut room vents to its steady state, `band_p` VACUUM, and stays a vacuum until a Vertical Slice plate install closes the hole (the same "room is lost" rule as a DESTROYED hull segment). With `n` holes of area A_CUT on a room of volume `V`: `k = G_OPEN × A_CUT × n / (V × GAS_SCALE)`; the room reaches DECOMP (`P` < 400) in `ceil(ln(1000/400)/k)` steps and VACUUM (`P` < 100) in `ceil(ln(1000/100)/k)` steps, `P0` 1000 dkPa nominal. `V` 20, `n` 1: `k` = 2 × 24 / 20000 = 0.0024; DECOMP `ceil(381.8)` = 382 steps = 2,292 ticks (38 s); VACUUM `ceil(959.4)` = 960 steps = 5,760 ticks (96 s). `V` 30, `n` 1: `k` = 0.0016; VACUUM `ceil(1439.1)` = 1,440 steps = 8,640 ticks. A room open to a larger connected volume vents more slowly (`k` uses the connected volume). Guarantees: no inventory lives in edges, so removing them creates or destroys nothing; power has no inventory; the current step's exchange across the seam is simply not computed; one notification batch with `T`, `S/<seam_id>`, affected `C/<id>`; the next run re-derives components. Cutting through a compartment is not a Graph operation and is not allowed (R10): a compartment belongs to one section and a cut never splits gas by a volume ratio. `discard_section(section_id)` (jettison, Web Map unload in VS-A) tombstones a section's slots; mass in it leaves the world and is added to the counters as `discarded_*` so the invariant still closes; ids are never reused.
223	
224	**LS-17 — Sections and dormancy.** Every node, edge and compartment carries `section_id`; a section record holds `kind` (HOME / DERELICT), `dormant`, `rate_pm` (LS-25), `stress_until_step`, the three conservation counters and `discarded_*`. A section is **dormant** when its derelict is not loaded (zoomed out, left behind): its slots are skipped by every phase, its atmosphere and failures stand still, its state is persisted and hashed unchanged, and it cannot be welded (`SECTION_NOT_LOADED`). The flag is written only by M19 `set_section_dormant` (Web Map & Transit at load/unload) and read through the pure `section(section_id)` → `{kind, dormant, rate_pm, stress_active}` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from web-map-and-transit)*. The section record also carries `dormant_since_step` (persisted; stamped when `dormant` is set); on load M19 also advances, by `step_no − dormant_since_step`, every subject's `mode_since_step` and non-zero `isolated_at_step` (GA-T, LS-14: a trail's age counts only the steps the section ran) **and** `warn_since_step` (while `has_warn`), `fail_since_step` (of every FAILED or DESTROYED subject) and `patched_at_step` (of every patched subject, `hp_cap` < `HP_FULL`), and every SeamRecord's `built_step` and `mode_since_step`, so the fairness gate never counts as served a warning the player never witnessed and a patch's decay clock does not run while the section sleeps; `stress_until_step` is deliberately not advanced (the breach rhythm's stress lapses while a section sleeps); then it sets `dormant_since_step` to 0 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. Loading it clears `dormant` and it resumes from its last state with no fast-forward (R13; SD OQ-2 resolved: cheapest, and a derelict that "does not degrade on its own" is the boarding rhythm GD asks for). VS-A (ADR-LSG-04): on unload the partition is serialised into Web Map's deltas and the slots are compacted away by an explicit order-preserving compaction mutator; reload re-creates them with **new** ids. Quiescence sleeping of islands (D.16) is the VS-A lever on top of dormancy, with its flag persisted so a restore resumes with the same awake set.

226	**LS-18 — Published mutators (M1–M19), two classes.** All are callable only inside a kernel-issued `WriteScope` in P2/P3, every signature takes the scope token first, and every one marks its dirty keys explicitly (packed-array element writes run no setter). **Class A** is command-backed: paired with a pure `check_*` used by the owner command's `validate`; `apply` is infallible once the check passed. **Class B** is the unconditional channel (kernel CR-9 path (a)): never rejects, clamps, and treats an unknown or stale id as a no-op returning 0/false. The Graph registers **no commands of its own**; the domain commands live with Assembly, Interaction, Suit, Emitter State and Horror (kernel H2).

Instruments' `load = ⌊1000 × demand / max(1, supply)⌋` is its own reading, not `ρ`, and reads no `cap`. `power_use(section_id)`, all in W per step for the section's consumers, recomputed in phase 2: `draw_w` = Σ served W (all tiers, lamps and inrush included, battery charge excluded); `delta_w_last5` = `draw_w` now − `draw_w` five runs ago (signed; lamps included — D.6 Example C's 1200 W contains its 300 W of lamps; `post_restore` seeds the window flat, so it reads 0 after a load); `lamps_lit_w` = Σ served W of LOAD subtype LAMP, including any LAMP node such as `bcn_main` (the Graph does not know a beacon, so its 20 W step is in `delta_w_last5` too); `noisy_w` = Σ served W of SCRUBBER, PUMP, HEATER and DOOR_MOTOR nodes (lamps excluded). `o2_pm`, `n_o2` and `n_inert` have no dirty-key quantum of their own: they ride the `C/<cid>` key fired by the `P` (10 dkPa) and `p_o2` (5 dkPa) buckets and stay exact in `read_view`.

256	**LS-20 — Dirty keys confirm `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS`.** Keys are ints `(KIND << 32) | id` with KIND ∈ {COMP 1, BAND 2, NODE 3, EDGE 4, DESC 5, LOOP 6, SEAM 7, TOPO 8, SECTION 9} (written in this document by their family names `C/<cid>`, `B/<cid>`, `N/<id>`, `F/<id>`, `L/<loop>/<anchor>`, `S/<seam_id>`, `T`, `SEC/<id>`); no String is built per key per run. Rules: continuous values never dirty per step — a key fires only when `⌊value / quantum⌋` changes bucket (quanta: `T` 1000 mC, `P` 10 dkPa, `p_o2` 5 dkPa, store 20 ‰, intensity 100 ‰, `hp` 250 bp); one `C/<cid>` per compartment per step, not one per field, fired when the `T`, `P` **or** `p_o2` bucket changed (three triggers, not `P` alone) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; structural change uses `T` + `SEC/<id>`, never per-node keys; last-emitted buckets are derived and `post_restore` seeds them so a restore yields one `ALL` and then silence; Instruments read values only through `perceived` and the honest needle moves on LS-20 quantum crossings as a one-step ramp (In-World Instruments IW-11); Failure & Trail polls once per Graph step and reads a per-step cache every frame (FT-15); Adaptive Audio reads per Graph step — keys wake discrete presentation only (trail spawn/despawn, loop on/off) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from in-world-instruments-and-inspect-view, failure-and-trail-system)*. D.10 bounds the worst designed cascade at 38 (MVP) and 135 (VS-A) keys, so **`MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256 stays as registered**; the Graph confirms it and asks that it never fall below 128 (MVP's worst case is 38; VS-A's 135 already exceeds 128) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. *Alternative considered:* SD's string-keyed families — the semantics are identical; the int encoding is chosen for the per-run allocation cost at VS-A (ADR-LSG-06) [UNV that the kernel's key type is Variant; if it is String, the family strings are the encoding and nothing else changes].

258	**LS-21 — Serialization, hash, summary, interchange.** *Persisted (canonical):* `schema_version`, `next_node_id`, `next_edge_id`, `next_seam_id`, `next_section_id`, `last_step_no` and the per-hook cursors `last_step_power`, `last_step_atmo`, `last_step_failure` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; the `def_table` CSR pair (`def_off`, `def_utf8`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; nodes and edges with every field of LS-3/LS-5 including tombstones; SeamRecords; sections with `dormant`, `dormant_since_step` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*, `rate_pm`, `stress_pm`, `stress_until_step`, `vented_mgu`, `radiated_dj`, `spilled_cool_ml`, `produced_mgu`, `breathed_mgu`, `produced_dj`, `burned_uml`, `spilled_heat_mdj` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, `discarded_*`, `withdrawn_*` (M16, per medium) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from web-map-and-transit)*; compartments `layout_room_ref`, `n_o2`, `n_inert`, `T`, `t_rem`, `fuel_puddle_ml` and the hysteresis memory `band_o2`, `band_p`, `band_t`, `p_prev` (the previous run's `P`), and the warn trackers `warn_since_o2`, `warn_since_p`, `warn_since_t` (i32 each) and `warn_bits` (u8) — canonical order after `p_prev` (+13 bytes per compartment, 65 for the MVP five) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; every stored OPENING's `strain_gas` and `strain_heat` live bits (SEAL_STRAIN hysteresis, D.14); **and the three input queues** — `pending_draw` (compartment, crew, mGU), `pending_load` (node, `req_w`) and `pending_trace` (kind, subject, magnitude), each in arrival order and bounded (draw ≤ `MAX_CREW` × compartments, load ≤ 64, trace ≤ `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP`), plus the last applied `draw_grant` table. A snapshot can be taken on any tick, so a queue that held a breath, a trace or a load change between two hook ticks would otherwise be lost on restore and the restored run would diverge from the uninterrupted one *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. *Derived, never in a snapshot:* `V`, `exposed_tiles` (from Layout), components, trees, `path_cap`, degrees, id → slot maps, `served_pm`, descriptors, `P`/`p_o2`/`o2_pm`, last-emitted buckets, the cached hash. Rule: anything the next step depends on that is not re-derivable from persisted fields is persisted (`t_rem`, `tc_rem`, `fuel_rem`, `out_w`, `forced_mode_next`, `warn_since_step` with its `has_warn` bit, `thaw_until_step` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, the GA-T fields `mode_since_step`, `mode_key` and `isolated_at_step`, `dormant_since_step` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*, the three `pending_*` queues, the band and SEAL_STRAIN memory, the compartment warn trackers `warn_since_o2/p/t` and `warn_bits` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*); `served_pm` is not, because phase 2 recomputes it before use. `canonical_bytes()` = the persisted fields in a fixed documented order, each as `[u32 tag][u32 length][field.to_byte_array()]`, raw slot arrays with tombstones — native memcpy, no interpreted loop. **`block_hash()`** is published: cached, recomputed only when the block was written since the last hash, H64 over `canonical_bytes()` (H64 = the first 8 bytes of the SHA-256 that native `HashingContext` returns, read as a little-endian u64 — a truncated hash, never a hand-rolled 64-bit mix) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; the kernel's `state_hash` is registered as `state_hash(scope, T) = H64( T || world_seed || concat over b in scope sorted by block_id of (len(block_id) || block_id || schema_version || len(canonical_bytes(b)) || block_hash(b)) )` with `block_hash(b) = H64(canonical_bytes(b))` cached per block and invalidated by the dirty bit, and the Graph's `canonical_bytes()` and `block_hash()` feed it unchanged *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)*. The one-level Merkle form (`state_hash` over per-block cached hashes, H64 via native `HashingContext` or S0-d's winner) is **kernel amendment K-1, routed to the kernel owner as an ADR candidate** and not a rule of this GDD (R5). **SHARED_SUMMARY** (VS-B): per compartment `T_dC` (int16, 0.1 °C), `P` (u16), `p_o2` (u16), three bands (3 bits each); per node/edge `state` (3 bits) + `sev` (3 bits) + `served_q` (0..15); per loop component `pool_q`; active descriptors compact `(id, mode, sev, alarm_eligible, intensity bucket = intensity_pm / 100, since_steps, mode_steps, grow_steps, each saturating at 2^24 − 1)` — 7 bytes for the first six fields plus 3 bytes for each of the two GA-T ages, 13 bytes each, from which a client derives `fail_since_step` and the trail's own age so two MIRROR crewmates see equal trail extent, dullness and density (CR-10, VS-B) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from failure-and-trail-system; GA-T fields added 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; seam list; about 0.4 KB at MVP, deltas ride the dirty keys; clients never receive `t_rem`, queues or RNG inputs — they receive truth, quantised. **Interchange (S-1, routed to Save/Load):** every Graph value stays below 2^53; the canonical form is packed int arrays; any JSON text form must carry the raw canonical bytes as base64 (`Marshalls.raw_to_base64`); `var_to_bytes` is not used — the `allow_objects` argument of the first draft is Godot 3-era and does not exist in 4.x, and Variant framing would put engine-version headers inside the hashed form *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; never a `Resource` for saves (R6; Godot JSON parses numbers as float — TD, sourced). Restore is two-phase (decode and validate into a scratch state, then swap); `restore(data, stored_version)` supports exactly version 1 in MVP, any other version is a reported failure, and every failure is a named `GRAPH_RESTORE_*` reason with the live state untouched (Section E). Type ids are append-only forever — the only forward-compatibility promise v1 makes.

260	**LS-22 — Falsifiability: perception-agnostic by construction.** No mutator argument carries a believed state; every argument is an id or a physical magnitude; the Graph never reads `PERCEPTION_OUT` (kernel CR-12) and `read_view` returns true values only, so a hallucinated "fixed" pipe (the Filter shows OK while `hp` = 2000) cannot change a Graph value and a hallucinated repair performs the real `repair_step` increments against the true `hp` — it costs time, not truth. Every gauge quantity has **one physical witness driven by the same Graph value**, so a lying instrument can be falsified by the world:
261	
262	| Gauge quantity | Physical witness (same value) | Channel (LS-14) *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)* |
263	|---|---|---|
264	| O2 pressure / fraction | `ATMO_THIN` band: breath audio and Suit's walk-only state (SE-27; no vignette) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from suit-and-equipment, sanity-and-hallucination-rules, perception-filter)*; scrubber hum via `served_pm` | consequence (Suit body cues, HUM_DROP at the scrubber) |

268	| Power | lamp brightness `served_pm`, hum pitch, relay clunk on STARVE | consequence (lamp brightness, HUM_DROP, CLANK); the breaker panel's own lamp is module-body |
269	| Coolant | pipe frost and drip descriptors, radiator glow, pump cavitation TICK | consequence (DRIP, frost trail, TICK); the radiator's glow sprite is module-body |
270	| Hull | hiss, debris stream, frost along the hole, groan TICK with `since_steps` | consequence (HISS, WIND, trail VFX, TICK) |

273	A WORN descriptor has no row: it is module-body and witnesses nothing. The witness of a worn machine is its falling output through D.4 (`out_scr`, `circ`, lamp brightness via `served_pm`) and, once a hazard mode takes over, that mode's consequence-channel descriptor. A PATCH_WEEP descriptor is on the consequence channel and witnesses the patch itself (`hp_cap < HP_FULL`): the Filter may repaint a patched module as whole, but may neither remove the weep nor add one to a sound module *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.

275	The headless test: set Perception output to "all OK" for a degraded fixture and assert `state_hash` of `graph.state` at tick N is identical with and without the Perception block's content (the kernel's own `PERCEPTION_OUT` pattern).
